uncertain.buildability: No vendor-hosted API exists, so I labelled not_buildable/local_only_tool. A toolkit could still self-host the CLI or call the Apify actor (netmilk/sherlock, whose .actor config lives in the official repo), which arguably makes it ready_with_caveats. This is a judgement call on rubric reading, not a factual gap.
uncertain.mcp: No MCP in the sherlock-project org (repo tree checked: no mcp files; org repos: sherlock, api, sherlockproject.xyz, build, .github). Apify auto-exposes the netmilk/sherlock actor via an MCP endpoint (apify.com/netmilk/sherlock/api/mcp, not opened). That actor was contributed by a third party (commit by GitHub user netmilk), so I treated it as community, not official.
uncertain.api_breadth: Effectively one operation (username lookup across ~400 sites). narrow vs none depends on whether a CLI counts as an API.

notes: Sherlock is an MIT-licensed Python CLI (PyPI sherlock-project, Docker sherlock/sherlock), not a service: no accounts, keys or hosted endpoint. The org has a stale 'api' repo (Django REST wrapper, last push 2021-07) that you have to self-host; it is not a public hosted API. Several unrelated projects are also called 'sherlock-mcp' (Fewsats domain-buying server, covertlabs infostealer intel, a .NET assembly analyzer), so name matching on MCP registries will give false positives. Burnsedia/sherlock-mcp is the real third-party wrapper for this tool. The pipx package is importable (package sherlock_project), but there are no documented library docs.
